name: Camino Francés
summary: The best-known road to Santiago, about 780 km from Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port over the Pyrenees and across northern Spain through Pamplona, Burgos and León. The high point is the Cruz de Ferro above Foncebadón; the terrain is walking rather than mountaineering, but it is walking every day for a month.

name: Camino Portugués
summary: The Central Way north to Santiago, walked by most people from Porto (about 240 km) though the full route starts in Lisbon. The one real climb is the Alto da Portela Grande de Labruja between Ponte de Lima and Rubiães; the duration and altitude given here are for the Porto start.

name: Camino Portugués Coastal
summary: The coastal variant of the Portuguese Way, about 274 km from Porto up the Atlantic shore through Vila do Conde, Viana do Castelo and Vigo before joining the Central route at Redondela. It stays low and has noticeably less climbing than the inland way.

name: Camino del Norte
summary: About 825 km along the Cantabrian coast from Irún through the Basque Country, Cantabria and Asturias before turning inland into Galicia. It never goes high, but the constant climbing in and out of coastal valleys makes it harder work than the Francés.

name: Camino Primitivo
summary: The oldest route to Santiago, about 320 km from Oviedo through the Asturian hills to Melide, where it joins the Camino Francés. The high ground is the Ruta de los Hospitales above Borres, an exposed 23 km ridge crossing with no villages or water; the lower Pola de Allande alternative tops out at the Puerto del Palo, 1,146 m.

name: Camino Inglés
summary: The short Galician route medieval pilgrims arriving by sea used, about 115 km from Ferrol through Pontedeume and Betanzos to Santiago. Its high point is A Malata on the long stage into Hospital de Bruma.

name: Via de la Plata
summary: The longest of the main routes to Santiago, roughly 1,000 km north from Seville through Extremadura and Salamanca, most walkers branching onto the Camino Sanabrés at Granja de Moreruela. Stages are long, villages are far apart, and the highest ground is the Padornelo pass on the way into Galicia.

name: Camino Finisterre
summary: The only Camino that starts in Santiago rather than ending there, about 90 km west through Negreira and Olveiroa to Cape Finisterre, with a further 27 km link to Muxía. The high ground is the moorland below Monte Aro.

name: GR20 Corsica Trek
summary: A 180 km traverse of Corsica's mountain spine from Calenzana to Conca, staying in staffed refuges. The northern half includes chains, scrambling and loose rock, and the high point is the Pointe des Éboulis under Monte Cinto.

name: GR10 Pyrenees
summary: The French side of the Pyrenees end to end, 866 km from Hendaye on the Atlantic to Banyuls-sur-Mer on the Mediterranean. It is waymarked throughout and drops into valley towns for resupply, but the cumulative ascent is very large and the high point is the Hourquette d'Ossoue below the Vignemale.

name: GR11 Pyrenees
summary: The Spanish Pyrenean traverse, about 800 km from Cabo Higuer to Cap de Creus, higher and emptier than the GR10 with around ten passes above 2,500 m. Snow lingers on the central section well into June; the high point is the Coll de Noucreus in Catalonia.

name: Amalfi Coast / Path of the Gods
summary: The Sentiero degli Dei, 7.8 km along the cliffs above the Amalfi Coast from Bomerano in Agerola to Nocelle, three to four hours and mostly downhill in that direction. The path is narrow and exposed in places, and finishes with a long stairway down to Positano.

name: Via Francigena
season: April – October, Alpine section roughly June – September
summary: The pilgrim road from Canterbury to Rome, over 2,000 km through France, Switzerland and Italy, following the stages Archbishop Sigeric recorded in 990. The only mountain crossing is the Great St Bernard Pass, which is normally free of snow for walkers from about mid-June.

name: Mallorca GR221
summary: The Ruta de Pedra en Sec, roughly 140 km the length of the Serra de Tramuntana from Port d'Andratx towards Pollença on old dry-stone mule paths. Days are long with a lot of ascent and descent, the high point is the Coll des Prat beside Puig de Massanella, and summer is too hot with unreliable water.

name: La Gomera GR132
summary: A circuit of about 127 km around the coast of La Gomera, usually split into eight stages from San Sebastián. It stays near the sea but the island's deep barrancos mean most days carry over 1,000 m of ascent and descent.
